topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, the scope of the cancer lecture series, and the specific learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Genetic, Endogenous, and Environmental Drivers of Cancer Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer etiology, contrasting endogenous mutational processes and inherited genetic predispositions with environmental exposures and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogens, Mutagens, and Tumor Promoters
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biological and molecular mechanisms by which specific chemical, physical, and infectious agents initiate DNA damage or act as tumor promoters to drive malignancy.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify mutational exposures and evaluate the carcinogenic potential of substances.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic provides concluding framing by summarizing the lecture's core themes and addressing real-world risk-benefit evaluations regarding carcinogen exposure.
